channel.title: Star Stuff
channel.description: Everything published on Star Stuff, newest first — 165 zines, field guides, broadsides, racks and working papers, each with the line it leads with. Subscribe by RSS, or read the changelog for the reasoning.
channel.copyright: CC BY-SA 4.0 · Stimpunks Foundation × More Realms

item.title: Almost All of It Is Holes
item.description:
Zine No. 100 — Young Readers

A read-aloud about a seed that flies on the parts that are not there — with something you can try, and every source kept on the page for the grown-up.

item.title: The Dog Breathes Out Sideways
item.description:
Zine No. 99 — Young Readers

A read-aloud about a nose that does not blow the smell away — with something you can try, and every source kept on the page for the grown-up.

item.title: Nobody Knows Where the Dog Came From
item.description:
Zine No. 98 — How We Got Here

On the first animal we ever domesticated, a skull that was a dog and then a wolf, two camps who stopped speaking, and a truce that produced a better answer than anyone wanted.

item.title: The Channel You Cannot Mask
item.description:
Zine No. 97 — Star Stuff

On four dogs, thirty-six strangers, 675 correct trials out of 720, and why the quiet room with the dogs is restful for a reason nobody flatters anybody by naming.

item.title: The Cuttlefish That Can’t See Colour
item.description:
Zine No. 96 — Young Readers

It matches whatever it sits on, it cannot see colour, and nobody has worked out how — read-aloud science for four to eight, with every source kept on the page where the grown-up can find it.

item.title: Bone Song, Read Aloud
item.description:
Zine No. 95 — Young Readers

Two true things about the bone inside your arm — the read-aloud door into Bone Song, Zine No. 1, which is where the argument lives.

item.title: Seeds That Wait
item.description:
Zine No. 93 — Young Readers

Some seeds do nothing at all when you plant them, and they are not broken — read-aloud science for four to eight, with every source kept on the page where the grown-up can find it.

item.title: The Colours You Cannot See
item.description:
Zine No. 94 — Young Readers

There are patterns on flowers that your eyes have no part for, and they are really there — read-aloud science for four to eight, with every source kept on the page where the grown-up can find it.

item.title: Two Things on One Leaf
item.description:
Zine No. 92 — Star Stuff

On thirty frogs in a stock tank that perch on absolutely everything, a leaf that is quietly moving several litres of air a day into airless mud, and the pairing we invented between them.

item.title: Nobody in This Pond Is Late
item.description:
Zine No. 91 — Young Readers

A frog changes, an axolotl never does, and both of them are grown-ups — read-aloud science for four to eight, with every source kept on the page where the grown-up can find it.

item.title: A Field Guide to the Sexes
item.description:
Field Guide No. 24 — Field Guides

Nineteen organisms sorted not by how strange they are but by which assumption each one breaks — because “there are two sexes and you are one of them” is five claims bundled together, and every one of them comes apart on its own somewhere.

item.title: Strike “His”
item.description:
Zine No. 90 — Star Gazing

On the kinky, poly, gender-fluid, queer sex lives of Terran life — what a fish does to its own cell memory in ten days, what a fungus does with twenty-three thousand mating types, and why none of it is the argument we were reaching for.

item.title: Nobody Set Out To Do This
item.description:
Zine No. 89 — Star Stuff

On a course held to better than a degree that nobody can explain, the ocean’s largest cargo carried by an animal that is not eating, and what it means that the missing account is ours.

item.title: Advice to a Young Marine Biologist
item.description:
Trigger No. 2 — Triggers

The ocean absorbed the heat and the carbon, and is now being billed for both.

item.title: What We Are For
item.description:
The Aims — Foundations

The mission of starstuff.earth, in eleven aims — each with the page where it is already being kept.

item.title: Which Distortion
item.description:
5 September 2026 — Glimmers

Nobody at any step became more accurate. They got better at choosing, and better at saying so.

item.title: The Name Was Already the Verdict
item.description:
Zine No. 88 — How We Got Here

On a record with no words that was banned for its title, a title the musician did not choose, and thirty years of engineering that had already decided a deviation from the specification was damage.

item.title: We Were Punk First
item.description:
Rack · One scene — Sound

Thirty-eight recordings of Indigenous punk, metal and hard rock — and the argument underneath them, which begins with a record that had no words in it and got banned anyway.

item.title: Overshoot
item.description:
Trigger No. 1 — Triggers

1.5 °C sounds small because it is an average of a planet that is mostly ocean.

item.title: Two Peppers
item.description:
Zine No. 87 — Star Stuff

On the point past which more light does nothing, one species that answered the same shade in two different ways, and what it takes to stop calling one of them a failure.

item.title: Edition Two
item.description:
4 September 2026 — Glimmer Wire

The week nothing could be opened, published saying so — and then amended when the block lifted.

item.title: Bird Minds
item.description:
Field Guide No. 23 — Field Guides

thirteen birds, sorted by what we wanted each one to prove

item.title: Older Than Either of Us
item.description:
Zine No. 86 — Star Stuff

On the right angles in a pigeon’s forebrain, three papers that disagree about where they came from, and what belonging looks like under either answer.

item.title: Six Principles and a Room
item.description:
An Essay — Foundations

An ethic you can only point at a person is an ethic that will keep finding the fault in the person.

item.title: The Lizard That Was Never There
item.description:
Zine No. 85 — How We Got Here

On a word that meant “border”, the diagram it turned into, and the eight years by which the refutation beat the bestseller.

item.title: Until There Were Ten
item.description:
2 September 2026 — Glimmers

A thing that never changes and has no counterexample is very hard to tell apart from a rule.

item.title: There Have Been So Many Earths
item.description:
Zine No. 84 — How We Got Here

Nine links from Theia to Chicxulub, with the state of the land drawn at each one — and the finding that only three of them were moments.

item.title: Edition One
item.description:
2 September 2026 — Glimmer Wire

Seven items filed on institutional press releases, because six publishers refused a direct read that day.

item.title: The Width of Itself
item.description:
Zine No. 83 — Star Stuff

On the root that opens a channel, the lawn that stays compacted, and why we keep asking survivors to do systems change.

item.title: Came Back Clean
item.description:
31 August 2026 — Glimmers

The pair that comes back clean is the one to worry about.

item.title: The Play You Keep
item.description:
Zine No. 82 — Star Stuff

On forty-five bumble bees, nine hundred and ten rolls of a wooden ball, and the definition science had to write down before it could see doing nothing at all.

item.title: None of Those Miles
item.description:
31 August 2026 — Glimmers

It’s happening. It’s really happening. It’s finally happening.

item.title: Flying Free
item.description:
30 August 2026 — Glimmers

I needed to witness something hopeful and wonder-filled, something to make me feel good about humanity.

item.title: Rainbow Serpents
item.description:
An Essay — Foundations

entropy increases in an isolated system — and the qualifier keeps falling off

item.title: Already an Entity
item.description:
Zine No. 81 — More Than Human

on a river that is a listed author, and a law that had to be asked

item.title: One Word for the Opposite
item.description:
Zine No. 80 — Star Gazing

On the vocabulary we built for what hurts, the single word we have for what doesn’t — and why a glimmer is probably not a dopamine hit, which is better news than it sounds.

item.title: Four Decimal Places
item.description:
Zine No. 79 — How We Got Here

A chain from atmospheric convection to a paperback subtitle — on the ratio at which a human life was said to begin going well, and the part-time student who read the primary source.

item.title: You Cannot Correct the Sky
item.description:
Zine No. 78 — Star Stuff

On why stars twinkle and planets do not, on knowing exactly where a problem lives — and on the fact that correct is not the same as affordable.

item.title: Nothing Melts
item.description:
Zine No. 77 — Star Stuff

On how snow grains bond below the melting point without ever becoming liquid, why the joint grows because it is the joint — and why bonding to each other does not fix what you are all standing on.

item.title: Forty Minutes to See
item.description:
Zine No. 76 — Star Stuff

On the second visual system, the forty minutes it takes to arrive, the one bright light that ends it — and the faint thing that only appears when you stop looking straight at it.

item.title: Under the Word
item.description:
Field Guide No. 22 — Field Guides

eighteen borrowed and invented words for Autistic joy, and what is actually holding each one up

item.title: The Mushroom That Cannot Be Farmed
item.description:
Zine No. 75 — Star Stuff

on the most expensive smell on earth, and the reason it is not in the mushroom

item.title: A Field Guide to Third Nature
item.description:
Field Guide No. 21 — Field Guides

a support nobody named is a support nobody defends

item.title: Oblivious to Encounter
item.description:
Zine No. 74 — How We Got Here

on what the plantation had to remove before it could scale, and the mushroom that has defeated seventy years of trying

item.title: Measured Against a Tree
item.description:
Zine No. 73 — Star Stuff

On six ways a moss fails as a plant, and the finding that the list is backwards — because holding your own water is the newer trick, and the tree is the one that lost the older one.

item.title: A Field Guide to Rainbows
item.description:
Field Guide No. 20 — Field Guides

there is no standard rainbow — and rarity, it turns out, is a fact about where the observer was standing

item.title: The Place Knows You’re There
item.description:
Zine No. 72 — More Than Human

on reciprocity, conditional belonging, and what a place asks of you that a room does not

item.title: Nothing Is Pushing
item.description:
Zine No. 71 — Star Stuff

On escape velocity as a coasting number, the places inside a well that cost nothing to sit in, and a telescope built so that it cannot brake.

item.title: Skepticism and Wonder
item.description:
Rack · One theme — Sound

The Rainbow Connection — forty songs, and the two uneasily cohabiting modes of thought they carry.

item.title: Both Arcs, One Drop
item.description:
Zine No. 70 — Star Stuff

On the raindrop that makes both bows at once, the lab that tried to erase both of you, and why entwined turns out to be a claim about the source rather than a feeling about the self.
